lead:
Headline inflation eased slightly to 15.39 per cent in August, and food inflation fell for the first time in six months, to 19.57 per cent.

The day in brief: the statistics bureau said cheaper palm oil, pepper, onions, yam flour and beef drove the food slowdown. Police issued a nationwide alert over intelligence that terrorists planned coordinated attacks on places of worship, schools and NYSC orientation camps, and two newly deployed mobile police officers were ambushed and killed in Benue. The NDLEA said it had dismantled another methamphetamine laboratory in Ebonyi and arrested a Mexican kingpin at Lagos airport. The TUC suspended action over King's College, Lagos, but education ministry unions insisted the concession be reversed. APC governors said they would back no arrangement that hurts President Tinubu's re-election, as Nyesom Wike defended his Rainbow Coalition. Aliko Dangote blamed smuggling for high petrol prices, the ADC said Nigerians were near the limits of endurance with petrol at N1,470, and AGRA said 36.3 million Nigerians face crisis-level hunger, the most of 17 countries it tracks.

items.h: Inflation eases to 15.39%; food inflation falls to 19.57%
items.s: The National Bureau of Statistics said headline inflation eased to 15.39 per cent in August from 15.43 per cent in July. Food inflation fell to 19.57 per cent from 20.31 per cent, its first decline in six months and well below the 25.30 per cent of August 2025, helped by lower average prices of palm oil, carrots, pepper, onions, cassava flour, beef and yam flour.

items.h: Police warn of terrorist plans to attack churches, mosques, schools and NYSC camps
items.s: Police headquarters put commands across the country on alert. A signal from the Force operations department, dated 13 September, said intelligence showed terrorists gathering for possible simultaneous strikes on churches and mosques, schools, NYSC orientation camps and other soft targets.

items.h: Two newly deployed mobile police killed in Benue ambush
items.s: Two mobile police officers newly deployed to Ayilamo in Logo local government, Benue, were killed in an ambush at about 6pm on Monday while on their way to escort the divisional police officer back to the community from Makurdi.

items.h: NDLEA arrests Mexican linked to Ebonyi meth lab
items.s: The NDLEA said it dismantled another industrial-scale methamphetamine laboratory in Ebonyi and that Mexican kingpin Arturo Carrera Loaiza, arrested on 19 August while trying to leave through Lagos airport, is linked to it. The agency said he was part of a network recruiting foreign experts to set up clandestine drug labs in Nigeria.

items.h: Education unions reject TUC's suspension of King's College strike
items.s: The TUC suspended its industrial action over King's College, Lagos, after Education Minister Tunji Alausa assured that no staff member would be dismissed or victimised. But unions in the ministry's Joint Workers Council, led by Abraham Onuche, rejected the suspension at a protest in Abuja and insisted the concession must be reversed.

items.h: APC governors reject any arrangement that undermines Tinubu
items.s: The Progressives Governors Forum said APC governors would neither join, support nor endorse any alliance that could undermine President Tinubu's re-election or harm the party's candidates in 2027. FCT Minister Nyesom Wike told Arise News the governors' position has no political basis, and a PDP faction warned them against undermining him.

items.h: Dangote blames smuggling for high petrol prices
items.s: Aliko Dangote told Arise TV that petrol prices remain high largely because the product is smuggled to neighbouring countries, where it sells for much more. His comments came after the refinery raised its gantry price and amid the crisis in the Middle East that has pushed up crude.

items.h: ADC says Tinubu has turned petrol pumps into punishment
items.s: ADC spokesman Bolaji Abdullahi said that with petrol selling for as much as N1,470 a litre, President Tinubu had pushed Nigerians close to the limits of human endurance, making every journey dearer and pricing food, electricity and even basic education out of reach.

items.h: AGRA says 36.3 million Nigerians face severe food insecurity
items.s: AGRA's August Food Security Monitor said 36.3 million Nigerians, 16.7 per cent of the population, face crisis-level food insecurity or worse, the highest number among the 17 African countries it tracks. It cited conflict, insecurity and displacement among the drivers.

items.h: Former northern governors form group to back Tinubu
items.s: Former governors Simon Lalong, Ibrahim Geidam, Ibrahim Shekarau and Abubakar Badaru are among northern leaders who concluded plans to unveil Arewa for Asiwaju, a platform to mobilise the North for President Tinubu's re-election. APC campaign director-general Abdulaziz Yari said the North has no reason not to support the President.

items.h: Obi's office says academics' endorsement is a plan to rig
items.s: Peter Obi's media office said the endorsement of President Tinubu by more than 600 lecturers from the 19 northern states and the FCT was “profoundly troubling” and part of a plan to rig the election. It asked INEC to bar pro-Tinubu academics from election duty and publish the names of prospective returning and collation officers.

items.h: Obi asks UNN to release his records and responds on Anambra loans
items.s: Peter Obi said on X that he has no objection to the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, releasing his certificates and records, insisting he has nothing to hide, after a suit sought certified copies of his credentials. He also responded to the Anambra finance commissioner's claim that loans from his tenure are still being repaid.

items.h: DMO raises N748.6bn at September bond auction
items.s: The Debt Management Office sold N748.64 billion of FGN bonds at its September auction, which featured a new ten-year bond maturing in 2036 and a reopened issue. Bids totalled N1.49 trillion, down 13.5 per cent from N1.73 trillion in August.

items.h: N728.97bn power sector bond closes
items.s: CardinalStone Partners, lead adviser and issuing house, announced the close of the N728.97 billion Series 2 Power Sector Bond, which takes the first phase of the government's programme to clear legacy power sector debts and improve liquidity to N1.23 trillion.

items.h: NYSC Batch C orientation to start on 30 September
items.s: The NYSC said the 2026 Batch C Stream One orientation course will run from Wednesday, 30 September, to Tuesday, 20 October, with corps members sworn in on 2 October, its spokeswoman Caroline Embu said.

items.h: Sokoto shuts mosque where cleric was stabbed
items.s: Sokoto shut the Musa Lukuwa Jumu'at Mosque in Mabera, in the state capital, after a fatal stabbing there, calling the building a crime scene. The government also named a panel of Islamic scholars to look into what lay behind the recent religious tension and recommend how to stop it happening again.

items.h: Nine passengers killed in Plateau bus attack
items.s: Gunmen opened fire on a commercial bus at Dungus Junction in Kuru, Jos South, on Sunday when the driver stopped to drop five passengers, killing nine people. The conductor, Nasiru Garba, was the only survivor; the bus, heading to Jos, was left riddled with bullets.

items.h: Ondo police arrest kidnappers collecting N1.5m ransom
items.s: Ondo police said they arrested suspected kidnappers as they collected a N1.5 million ransom, in an intelligence-led operation that also freed their victims.

items.h: Mining marshals uncover illegal gold mine in Abuja
items.s: NSCDC Mining Marshals arrested two suspects over an illegal gold mining operation in Gwagwalada Area Council of the FCT, acting on intelligence and a petition that unlawful mining was taking place within the coordinates of a valid exploration licence.

items.h: Shettima returns from BRICS summit
items.s: Vice President Kashim Shettima returned to Abuja on Tuesday after representing President Tinubu at the 18th BRICS summit in New Delhi, where he took part in high-level sessions and met Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

items.h: Tinubu welcomes Coca-Cola's planned $1bn investment
items.s: At the Nigerian Bottling Company's 75th anniversary event in Abuja, President Tinubu welcomed the Coca-Cola system's planned $1 billion investment in Nigeria over five years, which follows $1.5 billion in the previous decade, as a vote of confidence and said his government is making the business environment more predictable.

items.h: Minister hails Dangote IPO as market opens week higher
items.s: Trade Minister Jumoke Oduwole said the Dangote refinery IPO shows how regulatory reforms can improve access to capital for productive investment. On the first day of the offer the All-Share Index rose 0.10 per cent to 243,299.24 and market capitalisation reached N157.75 trillion.

items.h: Zulum backs Tax Ombud regional office in Maiduguri
items.s: Borno was designated the North-East headquarters of the Office of the Tax Ombud, and Governor Babagana Zulum promised to support the regional office in Maiduguri when he received a delegation led by Tax Ombud John Nwabueze.

items.h: PenCom extends verification as only 21% of civil servants enrol
items.s: PenCom extended the deadline for its mandatory online verification of federal employees with accrued pension rights from 31 July to 31 December 2026, after only about 21 per cent of an estimated 150,000 eligible workers had enrolled.

items.h: FG commits N10.5bn to train 32,000 in digital skills
items.s: Education Minister Tunji Alausa launched the N10.5 billion Digital Training Academy in Abuja to equip more than 32,000 young Nigerians with globally relevant digital skills, and Yaba College of Technology joined the programme.

items.h: Atiku camp predicts wins in 19 northern states
items.s: Kenneth Okonkwo, spokesman for Atiku Abubakar's campaign, told AIT's Democracy Today that the ADC candidate will win all 19 northern states and three in the South-West in the 2027 presidential election.

items.h: APM tells supporters to guard Makinde's votes
items.s: The Allied Peoples Movement urged Nigerians to stay vigilant and resist any attempt to deny its candidate, Oyo Governor Seyi Makinde, victory, saying his popularity among young people is a sign the party will win, spokesman Abubakar Yusuf said.

items.h: Radda and Inuwa reunite in Katsina APC
items.s: Former Katsina SSG Mustapha Inuwa returned to the APC after four years of criticising Governor Dikko Radda's administration, at a reception in his honour at Capital Hall, Katsina, and both men called for party unity.

items.h: Barau tells Kano North council to deliver all seats
items.s: Deputy Senate President Barau Jibrin inaugurated the APC's Kano North campaign council and told it to mobilise voters across the 13 local governments for victory “from top to bottom”, adopting “APC SAK” as the slogan.

items.h: Ex-minister says Eno instigated EFCC probe of Udom Emmanuel
items.s: John Akpanudoedehe, the ADC's Akwa Ibom governorship candidate and a former minister, alleged that Governor Umo Eno instigated the EFCC's actions against his predecessor Udom Emmanuel and officials of his administration. The state government called the claim false and provocative.

items.h: Disputes threaten ADC in Jigawa
items.s: Disputes threatened the ADC in Jigawa as governorship candidate Sabo Nakudu and party chieftain Bashir Jumbo clashed publicly over power sharing and candidate substitution, complicating the party's uphill battle against the ruling APC.

items.h: Six parties contest Kano Assembly by-election
items.s: INEC's resident electoral commissioner in Kano, Abdu Zango, said six parties will contest Saturday's Dawakin Kudu state assembly by-election, after a meeting of the inter-agency committee on election security.

items.h: Benin-Asaba road concessionaire promises faster work
items.s: The Benin-Asaba Expressway Concession Company asked motorists and communities along the 125km road for patience, saying construction will speed up after the rainy season. Chief executive Samuel Daramola said persistent rain had made work difficult.

items.h: Cally Air to expand fleet into 2027
items.s: Cally Air will take delivery of a CRJ aircraft, registered 5N-CRF, this September as part of a phased fleet expansion running into early 2027, adding capacity and flexibility across its network.

items.h: Nigeria resumes CAF A-licence coaching course after nine years
items.s: Twenty-five top-flight coaches began a two-module CAF A-licence course in Abuja on Monday, the first time Nigeria has hosted the course in nine years, marking its return to the CAF A-licence convention.

items.h: Nairobi to host 2029 World Athletics Championships
items.s: World Athletics confirmed at a council meeting in Budapest that Nairobi will host the 2029 World Championships, the first African city to do so, with Munich awarded 2031. Nairobi had previously bid unsuccessfully for 2025.
